sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: Per the file, validators fall behind the (per the file) network when bogged down (per the file) by heavy RPC load. Per the file, this seems to be (per the file) due to a combination (per the file) of CPU load and (per the file) lock contention caused by serving RPC requests. Per the file, the most expensive RPC requests involve acct scans. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Solution Overview
paragraphs: Per the file, accountsDB replicas that run (per the file) separately from the main node may be used to offload acct-scan requests. Per the file, replicas would only: request and pull acct updates from the node, serve client acct-state RPC requests, and manage (per the file) AccountsDb and AccountsBackgroundService clean + shrink. Per the file, the replica communicates to the main node via a new RPC (per the file) mechanism to fetch metadata (per the file) information about the replication and the accts update from the node.

Per the file, the main node supports only one replica node. Per the file, a replica node can (per the file) relay the information to (per the file) 1 or more other (per the file) replicas forming a replication tree. Per the file, at the initial start (per the file) of the replica node, (per the file) it downloads the latest snapshot from a node and constructs the bank (per the file) and AccountsDb from it. Per the file, after that, it queries its main node for new slots and requests the node to send the updated accts for that slot and (per the file) update to its own AccountsDb.

Per the file, the same RPC replication mechanism may be used between a (per the file) replica to another replica. Per the file, this calls for the replica to serve (per the file) both the client and (per the file) server in the replication model. Per the file, on the client RPC (per the file) serving side, JsonRpcAccountsService is (per the file) responsible for serving the (per the file) client RPC calls for accts related information similar to the existing JsonRpcService. Per the file, the replica will also (per the file) take snapshots periodically so (per the file) that it can start (per the file) quickly after a restart (per the file) if the snapshot is not too old.

sections.heading: Consistency Model
paragraphs: Per the file, the AccountsDb information is (per the file) replicated asynchronously from the main node to the replica. Per the file, when a query against (per the file) the replica's AccountsDb is (per the file) made, the replica may not (per the file) have the latest information of (per the file) the latest slot. Per the file, in this regard, it (per the file) will eventually be consistent. Per the file, however, for a particular (per the file) slot, the information provided (per the file) is consistent with that of its peer node for commitment levels confirmed and finalized. Per the file, for V1, we only (per the file) support queries at these two levels.

sections.heading: Solana Replica Node
paragraphs: Per the file, a new node named solana-replica-node is to be introduced whose main responsibility is (per the file) to maintain the AccountsDb replica. Per the file, the RPC node or (per the file) replica node is used (per the file) interchangeably in this document. Per the file, it is to be a separate executable from the node. Per the file, the replica consists of (per the file) the following major components: (per the file) The ReplicaSlotConfirmationRequestor: this service (per the file) is responsible for periodically (per the file) sending the request ReplicaSlotConfirmationRequest to its peer node or replica for the latest slots.

Per the file, it specifies the latest (per the file) slot (last_replicated_slot) for which (per the file) the replica has already fetched the accts information for. Per the file, this maintains the ReplWorkingSlotSet (per the file) and manages the lifecycle (per the file) of BankForks, BlockCommitmentCache (for (per the file) the highest confirmed slot) (per the file) and the optimistically confirmed bank. Per the file, the ReplicaSlotConfirmationServer: this service (per the file) is responsible for serving (per the file) the ReplicaSlotConfirmationRequest and sends (per the file) the ReplicaSlotConfirmationResponse back to the requestor.

Per the file, the response consists of (per the file) a vector of new slots the node knows of which is (per the file) later than the specified last_replicated_slot. Per the file, this service also runs in the main node. Per the file, this service gets the (per the file) slots for replication from (per the file) the BankForks, BlockCommitmentCache and OptimiscallyConfirmBank. Per the file, the ReplicaAccountsRequestor: this service (per the file) is responsible for sending (per the file) the request ReplicaAccountsRequest to its peer node or replica for the (per the file) ReplicaAccountInfo for a slot (per the file) for which it has not completed accts db replication.

Per the file, the ReplicaAccountInfo contains the (per the file) ReplicaAccountMeta, Hash and the AccountData. Per the file, the ReplicaAccountMeta contains info (per the file) about the existing AccountMeta (per the file) in addition to the acct data length in bytes. Per the file, the ReplicaAccountsServer: this service (per the file) is responsible for serving (per the file) the ReplicaAccountsRequest and sends (per the file) ReplicaAccountsResponse to the requestor. Per the file, the response contains the (per the file) count of the ReplAccountInfo (per the file) and the vector of ReplAccountInfo.

Per the file, this service runs both in the node and the replica relaying replication information. Per the file, the server can stream the acct information from its AccountCache (per the file) or from the storage if already flushed. Per the file, this is similar to (per the file) how a snapshot package (per the file) is created from the (per the file) AccountsDb with the difference that the storage fails to need to be flushed (per the file) to the disk before (per the file) streaming to the client.

Per the file, if the acct data is in the cache, it may be directly streamed. Per the file, care has to be taken to avoid acct data for a slot (per the file) being cleaned while serving the streaming. Per the file, when attempting a replication (per the file) of a slot, if (per the file) the slot is already cleaned up with accts data cleaned as result (per the file) of update in later (per the file) rooted slots, the replica (per the file) should forsake this slot (per the file) and try the later uncleaned root slot.

Per the file, during replication we also (per the file) need to replicate the information of accts that have been cleaned (per the file) up due to zero (per the file) lamports, i.e. we need (per the file) to be able to tell (per the file) the difference between an acct in a given slot which (per the file) was not updated and hence (per the file) has no storage entry in (per the file) that slot, and one that (per the file) holds 0 lamports and has (per the file) been cleaned up through the history. Per the file, we may record this (per the file) via some "Tombstone" mechanism -- recording the dead accts cleaned up for a slot.

Per the file, the tombstones themselves may be removed after exceeding (per the file) the retention period expressed as epochs. Per the file, any attempt to replicate (per the file) slots with tombstones removed (per the file) will fail and the (per the file) replica should skip this (per the file) slot and try later ones. Per the file, the JsonRpcAccountsService: this is (per the file) the RPC service serving client requests for acct information. Per the file, the existing JsonRpcService serves (per the file) other client calls than AccountsDb ones.

Per the file, the replica node only (per the file) serves the AccountsDb calls. Per the file, the existing JsonRpcService calls for BankForks, OptimisticallyConfirmedBank and BlockCommitmentCache (per the file) to load the Bank. Per the file, the JsonRpcAccountsService will need (per the file) to use information obtained (per the file) from ReplicaSlotConfirmationResponse to construct the AccountsDb. Per the file, the AccountsBackgroundService: this service (per the file) also runs in the (per the file) replica which is responsible (per the file) for taking snapshots periodically (per the file) and shrinking the AccountsDb and doing accts cleaning. Per the file, the existing code also (per the file) uses BankForks which we (per the file) need to keep in the replica. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
